meta.title: What income puts you in the global top 10% / 1% / 0.1%?
meta.units: international-$ per month (converted from daily at 365/12)
notes: The threshold is the average income of the marginal bin — the first bin at which cumulative population reaches the target share.
Population concept is basis-matched: adults for the per-adult series, total population otherwise — UN WPP adults 20+ and OWID population respectively, the same yardstick for every series.

thresholds.label: WID post-tax, rescaled to the ADJUSTED PIP country means (shape from WID, level from PIP_topadj — the far end of the PIP-side chain — so the bridge meets in the middle)
PIP on an income basis, top-adjusted (WID post-tax shape grafted above the splice bin, applied ON TOP of the consumption->income adjustment)
PIP adjusted to an income basis (consumption countries mapped via the dual-country regression)
PIP (disposable income or consumption, per capita)
